messages:
alex: Noticed a p99 tail blip on canary after the recent kernel-hint rollout. Looks like the excess is coming from host-side work (parsing/tokenize/writev) rather than decode.
maria: Which canary id? any quick traces?
ben: Can we get a flame graph? small changes in batching can surface weird I/O patterns.
alex: canary-3391123456. I sampled stacks during the spike, pasted below. Host CPU for ingress parse path up by ~22%.
```
  40%  runtime_proxy  ingress_proto_unmarshal
  25%  runtime_proxy  tokenize_loop
  12%  runtime_proxy  writev
  10%  libc.so       memcpy
  03%  runtime_proxy  kvcache_lookup
```
ciara: kvcache shows up but low. Did hit rate change?
maria: Yes, hit rate fell during the window: 0.81 -> 0.59. Evictions jumped as well. Metrics: 
```
  kvcache.hits: 810k -> 590k
  kvcache.requests: 1.0m -> 1.0m
  kvcache.evictions_per_min: 5.4k -> 28.3k
```
ben: Hmm. Coupling hypothesis: kernel selector tweak made minibatches smaller for short sequences -> more streaming fragments -> more frequent tokenization calls and more small writev syscalls -> worse syscalls + worse cache locality.
alex: We also saw avg-fragment-size go down: 1.1k -> 650 bytes, and writes/request increased ~1.6x. HTTP/2 framing plus our chunker amplify microwrites.
ciara: Can we validate causality? Options: (1) revert kernel hint in canary, (2) apply temporary fragment coalescer that waits up to 150us or until 1k bytes, (3) increase kvcache size on canary and see if p99 recovers.
maria: I like (2) for fast feedback. I'll add a lightweight coalescer in the sidecar that merges small ingress buffers. Low risk and quick to A/B.
ben: I'll prototype the coalescer. Replay harness command: `./tools/replay --trace=ingress --canary=3391123456 --enable-sidecar-coalesce --iters=1000`
alex: If coalescer restores fragment distribution and kvcache hit ratio, then we know fragmentation is driving the regression. If not, we dig deeper into kernel batch boundary edges.
ciara: Also adding perf counters to track fragment-size histogram and write syscalls per request in the canary so we can graph the delta.
maria: Quick note: there's a small memory-pressure blip on these nodes that correlates with higher eviction rate; not sure if it's cause or effect. Might be GC or per-request buffers not being reused.
ben: I'll check allocator traces during the replay runs. If coalescer helps but memory pressure remains, we need to look at buffer pooling too.
alex: Deploy-bot, hold the rollout while we test.
deploy-bot: Canary canary-3391123456: rollout paused (requested by alex) 6a7
alex: Timeline: ciara lands sidecar coalescer on canary tomorrow 09:30 PT, ben runs replay and posts flamegraphs + kvcache metrics, maria correlates p99/regressions. If fixed, decide between a kernel-selector rollback or permanent coalescer + follow-up tests.
ciara: On it. I'll post perf tarball and quick diff charts here after the run. :mag_right:
ben: test command I'll run: `./tools/replay --replay=/captures/3391123456 --enable-coalesce --num-iter=500 --out=artifacts/3391123456-coalesce.tar`
maria: Adding note to the incident tracker with initial findings and hypotheses.
alex: Thanks team. Keep the kernel-selector PR open but add an experimental flag so we can gate it while we sort host-overhead interactions.
